about: Own-words reads from the daily research task (ADMIS, Rabobank, Czapp and the news feed). fund_score: -1 bearish to +1 bullish, a judgement on the fundamental news only.

events: Weekly US export sales were the best in seven weeks (all 2026/27), led by Vietnam; shipments slowed. Commitments run ahead of last year but behind the 5-year pace vs USDA (ADMIS).
A weaker dollar after the midterms and hopes of lower tariffs helped early in the week; equity weakness capped mill-demand optimism (ADMIS).

sugar.fundamental: Still no fresh centre-south crush data; India's fast start remains the dominant supply signal. Yesterday's crude-led short covering looks fragile now that oil is sliding again on peace hopes, which trims the ethanol-parity cushion under Brazilian mills.
events: Raw sugar's midweek bounce came from short covering tied to crude rather than any change in Brazil's cane outlook (Barchart).
Crude turned lower Thursday as Iran and Ukraine peace optimism grew, removing the prop behind sugar's rebound (OilPrice.com).
India's early and quick crush is still the main bearish factor for the new season (ADMIS, Barchart).

coffee.fundamental: The deliverability story is strengthening: ICE certified arabica keeps climbing as Brazilian lots clear grading, and that exchange supply is what is pressing Dec and March lower. With Brazil shipping briskly and rains helping next year's crop, there is little on the supply side to slow the slide near term.
events: Arabica fell again as ICE certified stocks and wider global supply weigh on the nearby (ADMIS, Barchart).
Brazil-origin lots dominate the arabica grading queue, pointing to more certified-stock builds ahead (ADMIS).
Brazil's October exports ran well above last year while Colombia's output slipped (ADMIS).

cocoa.fundamental: A new supply risk offsets part of the stock build: Ivory Coast's weather agency warned El Niño could cut national output by as much as a quarter, which lands as port arrivals already lag badly. Prices bounced about 4% on short covering, but ICE certified stocks are still at an 18-month high, so the bearish exchange picture has not gone away.
events: Ivory Coast's meteorological agency warned El Niño could reduce cocoa production by up to 25% (Reuters).
Dec cocoa jumped ~4% intraday on short covering after breaking to its lowest since June (Barchart, ADMIS).
ICE cocoa stocks keep building to their highest since May 2024 while Ivorian arrivals trail last year (ADMIS, Reuters).
